card.name: Patients after pediatric or elderly
card.fires_on: The word "patients" right after "pediatric" or "elderly" in label headings and sentences, such as the Pediatric Use statement. It also fires on small words like "use" or "in" that come before patients or a drug combination.

modes.label: Pediatric patients
modes.description: The word patients after "pediatric" in the standard safety-and-effectiveness sentence.
modes.example: Pediatric Use Safety and effectiveness in pediatric<< patients>> have not been established.

modes.label: Linking words before patient groups
modes.description: Words like "use" or "in" that lead into a patient group or a combination.
modes.example: Discontinuation of desvenlafaxine should be considered<< in>> patients with symptomatic hyponatrem

modes.label: Elderly patients warning
modes.description: Patients after "Elderly" in a boxed warning heading.
modes.example: BOXED WARNING Increased Mortality in Elderly<< Patients>> with Dementia-Related Psychosis Elder

card.writes: It seems to push toward group or team nouns, and away from words like project or situation.
card.plain: It lights up on the word "patients" when a label talks about a group such as children or the elderly.
